hand.status: Written here before implementation; neither candidate fixtures nor product were executed
hand.representation: Arrays below mean exact ASCII lines joined by LF with a final LF. Empty strings are actual blank clock lines.
hand.timeDerivation: Hand integer Gregorian calendar offset from 1980-01-01 to 2026-10-29 00:00:00 plus one 100ns tick; this is the existing GPST calendar coordinate, not GPS-week zero or UTC.

legacy.note: LegacyEpoch omits an absent receiver_clock under its derived serializer. Nested ObservationValue uses its explicit ToJson and retains lli/ssi as JSON null; neither wire convention is changed.

hand.lateTruncation: Extend either handwritten stream with a later initialized descriptor but omit its clock/observation tail. The earlier valid RNX prefix may exist only as .part; native finish fails and no complete delivery or downstream result is allowed.
hand.recoveryLoss: Three initialized modern epochs: first valid, second has an invalid observation token at a known boundary, third fully reinitializes. With recover=true expect native complete=false, acceptable=false, epochs=2, recovered_epochs=1 and the original crx-unsynchronized error finding; no qualified publication.
hand.ioIdentity: Successful short writes must reconstruct the exact handwritten LF output. A partial write followed by injected EIO, input mutation, output readback mismatch or output budget exhaustion cannot produce a complete receipt; byte identities are actual or unknown.
hand.futureFreeze: Before implementing, freeze full handwritten CRX/RNX files and standard-library hashes. Preserve any malformed authored fixture separately; never derive expected values/format from a new product run or loosen expectations.

budget.kind: Independent byte-count/prefix formula plus frozen unchanged-base canonical wire SHA, not a new-decoder numerical oracle
budget.wireEvidence: Zero is the fixed accepted-base .000 spelling, independently verified as Decimal zero in a 14-byte field. Budget byte counts remain independent; SHA is a frozen base-wire copy oracle, not a new decoder oracle.
